- When sentiment is positive (≥0.3) and model forecasts are significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) and model forecasts are below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 10–15% in next 3–5 days to allow mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.0–0.2) and model shows persistent upward bias, apply downward adjustment to align with recent mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the cycle; apply 3–5% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.0–0.2), model tends to underreact; increase forecast slightly to avoid missing downward trend.
